_note: The battle royale's match rules that are not the ring's (src/config/ring.json) and not the loot's (src/config/loot.json): how many share a squad, the care package's arrival, the loadout crate and Storm Surge. Apex publishes almost none of this, so nearly every number here says it is ours; the two that are published are cited where they sit.
_teams: Solo, duos and trios, Apex's three squad sizes. `size` is how many share a squad. `bots` is the bot counts the lobby row offers for a match played alone, and every one of them is a count where 1 + it divides by the squad size, so the lobby is whole squads: a solo match is not a trio match with two gaps in it, which is what item 46 of docs/NEXT_STEPS.md is about. `bleed` scales the bleed-out clock in src/config/squad.json: a duo has half the time to be picked up because there is only ever one person who can come, and a solo has no bleed-out at all because there is nobody. Ours: Apex runs the same 90 s in every size.
_defaultTeam: what the lobby opens on, and what a match built before there were sizes is
_pod: The care package's arrival (item 32). It used to appear at 120 m with a dim beam, fall in silence and print one line of text. Now it is called first: a notice and a squad ping name the place it is coming down on, `announce` seconds before it appears, so everyone can start moving. It falls under a canopy trailing smoke, thumps down in a ring of dust, and stays lit and marked for `contest` seconds, which is the window the fight over it happens in. `height` is where it comes in from, unchanged. The fall time itself is loot.json's podFall, which the package already had. Apex announces its packages 4:05 before the ring closes and lands them 2:30 before (docs/RESEARCH_PHASE_11.md section 15); ours is that shape scaled to a ten-minute match, and every number below is ours.
_podHeard: How far the horn when it is called and the thump when it lands carry, metres, for the page that plays them (src/main.ts, through onRemoteFx). The delay comes for free from the 343 m/s speed of sound the audio already models. Ours.
_podLure: A bot inside this many metres of a package that is falling or still in its contest window goes for it instead of walking its graph. Without this nobody contests a care package but the squad, which is the whole of what makes one an event. Ours.
_loadoutPod: The loadout crate (item 24): the drop that hands you the loadout you built on the Loadouts tab, the way Warzone does it. It comes down in the late rings, one per phase listed, and it serves the whole lobby: each player claims their own guns out of it once, so a squad mate taking theirs does not empty it. `phases` are the ring's phases counted from 0, so 1 and 4 are the second and the fifth rounds. The guns arrive kitted to `mag` and `rarity`, fitted from the same preference list the Hot Zone's kitted gun uses (loot.json kitted.prefer), because a second list of preferences would drift from the first. It falls for loot.json's podFall like the care package does. `inset` keeps it well inside the ring it is called into. Ours: Warzone publishes none of this.
_surge: Storm Surge (item 34). The ring only hurts you outside it, so a squad that sits in the middle of the safe zone is never punished and hiding wins ties. From `fromPhase` on, when more players are alive than the phase's share of the lobby allows, everyone is ranked by the damage they have dealt and the ones below the line take a tick of damage wherever they stand, on the ring's own 1.5 s clock. `alive` is that share, one per ring phase: 1 means everyone may live, so the early rounds never surge. `minAlive` is the floor, so the surge never tries to thin a lobby that is already down to a fight. `warn` is the countdown before the first tick, and the surge cancels if enough people die during it. `grace` spares anyone who has dealt damage that recently, because the rule is aimed at hiding and not at losing a fight. `damage` escalates one step every `stepEvery` seconds it stays live. Ours: Apex has not published its thresholds, and ours are fractions of the lobby rather than counts so they hold for a lobby of four as well as one of twelve.
